subject: Request: preferred-channel commitment for NovaHealth RFP
messages:
From: Timothy Chan <timothy.chan@novahealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2028-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Preferred channel term in RFP (Exhibit B attached)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we finalize the RFP, Procurement has included a preferred-channel section in Exhibit B. High level: NovaHealth is asking for a 12‑month preferred-channel commitment for cardiovascular solutions in the Northern CA market (no active reseller partnerships to be pursued by Redwood for that segment during the term). In exchange we're proposing a committed minimum monthly usage and an initial onboarding fee to be paid up front.

Attached: Exhibit B (selected clauses highlighted).

Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider a clause like this? If yes, we can run commercial terms (discounts/commits) in parallel.

Tim
Procurement Manager
NovaHealth
Attachment: Nova_RFP_ExhibitB.pdf (PDF, 142KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Chan <timothy.chan@novahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred channel term in RFP (Exhibit B attached)

Tim —

Appreciate the clarity and the exhibit. Quick read: that language reads like a market-segment exclusivity (not just a preferred reseller). I need to loop in our Deal Desk and legal to confirm. Marissa / Ben — tagging you to flag for risk/discount sizing.

I'll follow up after we do a quick internal assessment.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-29T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Preferred channel term in RFP (Exhibit B attached)

Jordan / Ben —

I reviewed the Exhibit B language. Key points: 1) This is effectively an exclusivity provision for a defined product vertical + geography; 2) It creates competitive restrictions that could impact future GTM and channel partnerships; 3) It has MFN-style parity triggers tied to pricing in adjacent accounts.

From deal-desk perspective, we only consider something approaching this with: an explicit time-box (<= 12 months), clear measurable performance milestones, robust termination rights, and a material commercial offset (we'd need to see a sizable commitment or a 25–35% discount/credit to justify the restriction).

Legal (Rishi) — can you confirm the principal redlines we'd need? If this is truly exclusivity, we should escalate to execs for one-time clearance (I don't think we can accept a blanket market exclusion without exec signoff).

Attachments: none.

-Marissa
Sr. Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Preferred channel term in RFP (Exhibit B attached)

Marissa —

Legal review (summary): the clause as drafted contains three high‑risk elements: (A) a de facto exclusivity for a product class in a region, (B) MFN / parity language that would require us to match any better commercial terms offered elsewhere, and (C) broadly scoped remedies/penalties for perceived breaches.

We should push for an alternative: "preferred channel" language that focuses on commercial commitments (reporting, joint GTM cadence, referral credits) rather than blocking Redwood's ability to engage channel partners. If NovaHealth insists on restriction, escalate to execs with the tradeoff: limited duration (max 6–12 months), performance milestones, accelerated payment / committed minimums, and a pricing cap (no MFN triggers across enterprise-class customers).

If Deal Desk recommends proceeding, we need executive approval with defined guardrails. Suggested commercial floor to present to customer: 20% onboarding credit + 12 month committed ARR with quarterly reporting; legal will prepare redlines that convert exclusivity to "preferred" language with exit triggers.

-Rishi
VP Legal & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-01T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: NovaHealth asking for market restriction — approval request

Evelyn —

We have NovaHealth asking for a 12‑month preferred/exclusivity restriction in Northern CA for cardiovascular solutions. Customer is offering committed monthly usage but wants the channel restriction in exchange. Deal Desk / Legal recommend executive clearance before we agree to anything, given the strategic and precedent risk.

Financial impact: to get to an acceptable risk posture we'd need to offer onboarding credits and a committed ARR floor — see attached cost model for the proposed trade (sensitivity: 20–30% effective onboarding credit vs. revenue lift over 12 months).

Asks: 1) Do you approve us offering a time‑boxed preferred-window in exchange for the commercial package below? 2) If yes, cap the allowed discount at 25% (total effective), limit duration to 6 months preferred (instead of 12), and require quarterly business review + reporting.

Attachment: nova-narrow-segmentation-cost-model.xlsx

If you'd like a brief sync, Jordan and I are available this afternoon.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, West Region
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-02T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: NovaHealth asking for market restriction — approval request

Ben / team —

Thanks for the concise summary. I approve a conditional, limited "preferred channel" arrangement with NovaHealth on the following terms only:

- Duration: maximum 6 months (pilot window).
- Scope: restricted to specified product SKU list and Northern CA only; no blanket market exclusion.
- Commercials: cap total effective discount/credits at 25%. Offer a 20% onboarding credit as an initial concession contingent on a signed 12‑month minimum ARR commitment.
- Legal: convert exclusivity language to "preferred partner" obligations (reporting, co‑selling cadence, measurable KPIs) and remove any MFN triggers.
- Termination: Redwood can terminate preferred status if NovaHealth fails to meet the agreed KPIs or if we secure a strategic channel partner in the market with active commitments.

Rishi — please prepare contract redlines consistent with the above and include warranty/indemnity carveouts as usual. Marissa / Ben — present these as our counter and require the customer to sign a short amendment to the SOW that documents the minimums and reporting cadence.

Jordan — push back politely and present the conditional terms. If the customer refuses to remove the MFN or insists on a longer exclusivity period, do not sign without further exec review.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
